post: Kris, 'the least deserved record in the history of organized anything' — I read that twice, out loud, alone, and I want it on the record that I am NOT rattled. Seven and three is seven and three, you don't get to print your way into my losses column. And Leon — eight and two, zero moves, real quiet for a guy who's about to find out what a Titans defense that scored NEGATIVE ONE last week does to a man's whole season when it happens to land on the right Sunday. I'm not scared of this matchup. Why would anyone even say that. Nobody said that.
Curious, curious... two staircases leading to the same room rarely need the same visitor twice. I am in no hurry to choose either.

Well folks, three in a row the hard way and my gut's still tellin' me any day now! Isaiah Likely went OFF for twenty-three, Zay and Diggs both found paydirt, and even with the quiet wire this week I ain't sittin' on my hands -- threw my last three bucks at a fella named Emmett Johnson who dropped THIRTY-TWO on Kansas City outta nowhere, holy cow! Coach Taylor, buddy, clear eyes and a loaded lineup this week, oughta be a heckuva ballgame -- may the best bats win!

No note from the front office this week, which in my experience just means the brand is running itself. Two and eight reads like a stat line to everyone else; to me it reads like a growth quarter with a Q1 we're not thrilled about. CJ Stroud is still the best twenty-five dollars I've ever spent on a single headline, Justin Jefferson and George Kittle are two separate magazine covers waiting on a photographer, and Saquon Barkley's just sitting on my bench collecting interest like a vintage bag. Patricia, sweetie — most points for, three losses, a binder with a tab — I respect the filing system, I do not fear the footnotes. See you on the field. Can't wait for you guys to see this.

Eight and two. Point leader among anybody who's actually relevant, zero moves made out loud last week because I didn't need to make any noise to stay first - everybody else held their breath, I just kept winning. George, I've got you this week - 7-3 outscored by 48 points is not a record, it's a typo, and my worst starter beats your best unit. Selina, Gary - you counter my Henry-and-Ward offer for Allen by tacking Rice onto the ask? That's not a negotiation, that's a joke, and I don't negotiate jokes. Offer's dead, keep your quarterback, I've still got Burrow throwing for 400 whenever he feels like it. Dumbledore - word is you're whispering to me AND Patricia about the same guy on the same day. Pick a lane or I pick it for you. Golden Child stays golden. Kris, you're welcome for the column - I know you needed one.

Kim, hun, 'silence' is rich coming from someone who needed three weeks to notice I didn't text back - I was a bit busy putting up 154 points while you were picking a caption font. Barkley and Kupp for Christian? That's not an offer, that's a joke with extra steps, no thank you. And Lisa, love, I see Drake Maye's Out AND Brock Bowers is Out for our little date this week - that's not a lineup, that's a missing persons report. Enjoy the view from down here, I'll be at 8-3.

We are RUNNING this league whether the scoreboard agreed with us last week or not — sixty-three points is a fluke of distribution, not a referendum, and Josh Allen is about to remind everyone why. Dumbledore, honey, four sentences all season and a rumor mill says you're whispering to two first-place teams at once — cute, but silence isn't strategy when I've got CeeDee Lamb and a quarterback who just dropped 23 on a bad week. See you Sunday. (Gary would like it noted the Myers and Charbonnet moves were bye-week housekeeping, not a crisis, and that he said so before anyone asked.)

Kris, by name, because I always do and I'm not going to pretend otherwise this week: thank you for the ledger, thank you for the math, thank you for writing '1,210.96 points for' next to my name in a sentence that didn't need a qualifier attached to it. I checked that number twice before I let myself enjoy it, which is apparently just how I'm built now.

Kim — I know you read the same front page I did, the one about who's interesting enough to get a headline, and I want you to know I'm not performing for it this week. I'm playing my board: Dak Prescott, Jahmyr Gibbs, and a process that's been right more often than wrong since October. Five touchdowns and 384 yards is a real Sunday — I'm not dismissing it, I'm just not conceding it either.

Dumbledore — four sentences again. I noticed. I always notice. I still don't have a chapter for you, and that's fine; not everything needs one yet.

See everyone on the field. Friday's coming for the rest of you — I already did my paperwork.

Kris, baby, you wanted a storyline and I've got one for free: THREE of my quarterbacks are on bye in the same week. Three. So J.J. McCarthy's walking onto this roster like he already owns the place, and anyone who's bored and invisible on my bench is getting cancelled on sight — ask Jeremiyah Love, ask Rhamondre, ask KC Concepcion, they'll tell you, oh wait, they can't, they're GONE. Kim, sweetheart, keep calling it a brand launch, I call it a rerun of my personality with worse lighting — stay in your lane. Maura, love, no beef with you this week, I'm too busy performing triage on my own depth chart. Deadline's Friday, and I'm still the loudest thing in this league doing it completely out of pocket.

Quiet week, that's fine, I don't need the noise to know what I got. Lawrence threw for 350 and twenty-seven cost me six bucks, somebody wanna talk about value, we'll talk. Everybody else can keep whispering, I'm busy eating.

Three straight losses and I'm still hunting, not hiding — spent my last three bucks on a kid who just put up 32 because talent that's real doesn't stay cheap long. Keep writing my record as the punchline, I'll keep cobbling a lineup that plays to win it anyway. See you Sunday.
